[b] Defense in my Tower? More Strategy than you think. [/b] TDS is probably one of the greatest Tower Defences and RTS games of all time. The complexity and depth of the game comes from the interactions between the maps and your Vessel (character / class). The game starts out simple enough but the difficulty quickly ramps up, leaving you to be overrun quickly if you don't know what you're doing. It has hundreds of hours of content already in early access, with endless replayability as you try different strategies. TDS is also a very beautiful game with the simplistic yet pleasant design, with different maps harnessing different aesthetics. The unique OST also begins soothing but quickly becomes evermore intense as you progress through the Tides. The game truly shines as an amazing multiplayer game, where you can play with up to three of your friends. The real fun in multiplayer is synergising your Vessels and Towers to create interesting (and sometimes broken) combinations. I do agree that the campaign interface can sometimes be tedious, and you have to spend a lot of time to make sure that you haven't missed any parts. There's also an issue in the lack of clear information in what some tower upgrades and cardinals actually do, leaving you to experiment for a long time. The developer is extremely active and accessible through the studio's discord, posting daily updates of his progress. The modding scene although in its infancy, shows some amazing potential to create some great additions or even overhauls to the game. With 2 major updates and countless other small ones in the future, the game has a bright future ahead. Overall, a must try if you're a lover of either the Tower Defence or RTS Genres.

As a tower defense game, TDS stands above many of its competitors as a unique and challenging strategy experience. However, this game struggles to get a hold on new players due to its lack of handholding, complex gameplay, and its tedious UI. It might be hard to pick up at first, but giving this game some time will let you realize how amazing it truly is, whether that be with friends or alone.

I'm impressed by the amount of replayability this game offers, as well as how much content is currently in it. Each map has various puzzles that you can utilize to make the challenge a bit easier, depending on your current character(vessel). These are skippable, but it provides for a unique twist on every single map. Did I mention there's a ton of maps? It's set up in a way that encourages players to backtrack to unlock more on maps they weren't previously able to advance on. So far, I've only unlocked two vessels and they're so vastly different from each other that I may as well be playing a different game! (Impressive) Co-op has been fun, and brings about its own challenges and rewards as well, such as mine placement. Overall, it's probably the most creative tower defense game I've played, it's challenging, and so far I'm not even a fourth of the way through all of the achievements as a gamer at 10 hours. I wouldn't be opposed to an infinite map, or an easy-to-use map designer as well. 10/10 as far as tower defense goes. I'm looking forward to more maps and more characters, hopefully the developer continues to work on this for a while.

I really want to like this game — it has a beautiful aesthetic and a promising concept. Visually, it can be stunning, and the core tower defense gameplay is enjoyable… when everything’s working smoothly. Unfortunately, I’ve struggled a bit with the controls and overall interface. The world map feels disorienting, and I often find myself accidentally navigating it when I’m just trying to interact with tower defense levels. Important visual elements can be hard to see or interpret, which makes traversal and planning more frustrating than it should be. In combat, the difficulty curve feels inconsistent. I can have a solid setup with decent towers, only for a sudden spike — like a Tide 9 or Tide 11 wave — to wipe out a significant portion of my defenses with little warning or time to adapt. Maybe this improves when playing cooperatively, but as a solo player, it feels punishing rather than challenging. The user interface also has some quality-of-life issues that really wear on me over time. Pressing ESC always opens the settings menu, regardless of context — it doesn’t back out of the current screen, which breaks common UI conventions. Right-clicking also doesn’t return to the previous screen, forcing me to click a distant, sometimes hard-to-see “Back” button in the left side of the screen. It’s a small thing, but it adds up. Finally, while this is subjective, the music doesn’t do much for me — it’s oddly sleepy and doesn’t seem to complement the action or aesthetic in a meaningful way. There’s a lot of potential here, and I haven’t given up on it entirely, but in its current state, it feels more frustrating than fun. With more polish and attention to the player experience, this could really shine.

玩了三十多个小时，神中神的好游戏。它表面上挂着“塔防”名号，真正玩起来却像把传统 TD 和小型 RTS 硬塞在一起：地图没有既定路线，你得亲自操控名叫 Vessel 的角色在战场里奔跑、补塔、嘲讽怪物，敌人还会回头拆你防线，整局都得随时动脑又动手。每一波 Tide 涌来，都要精心考虑布置——尤其多人联机时。 每一个角色的机制和体验完全不一样，各有优劣，需要根据关卡即使调整，也要考虑和朋友之间相互配合，很难给人玩腻了的感觉，希望官方之后还会继续更新新角色。 局内音乐听着很舒服，电气管弦混编的 BGM 在局里越打越带感，非常爽。 画风非常喜欢每一关的差异化也非常明显，可以感觉到下了不少功夫在关卡设计上。 更难得的是开发者的用心：刚刚结束 EA、在 2025 年 5 月 23 日上线 1.0 “YELLOW”补丁时就顺带加了十几种语言、本体立减 40%。游戏虽然还是小体量，巅峰在线不过九十来人，但你能明显感觉到制作组在一点点填坑、扩张宏图；官方社区每条更新日志都洋溢着“谢谢大家陪我”的笨拙热情，看得人跟着嘴角上扬。 总结：神中神的好游戏买了血赚，和朋友一起玩爽飞飞。 Played for over thirty hours, an extremely good game that truly deserves its "Godly" title. It pretends to be a "tower defense" game on the surface, but when you actually play it, it's like blending traditional TD and small-scale RTS together: the map has no set routes, you have to personally control the character named Vessel to run around the battlefield, repair towers, taunt monsters, and the enemies will even come back to attack your defense line. Throughout the entire game, you need to constantly use your brain and take action. Every wave of Tide coming in requires careful planning - especially when playing multiplayer online. The mechanics and experiences of each character are completely different, each having its own advantages and disadvantages. They need to be adjusted according to the levels, and also need to consider cooperating with friends. It is difficult to make people feel bored. We hope the developers will continue to update new characters in the future. The in-house music is very pleasant to listen to. The electronic orchestral blend background music becomes more and more exciting as it keeps playing in the office, and it's really enjoyable. The game style is very fond of the distinctiveness of each level, and it is quite obvious. One can sense that a lot of effort has been put into the design of the levels. What's even more remarkable is the dedication of the developers: Just after EA was completed, on May 23, 2025, the 1.0 "YELLOW" patch was released, which incidentally included over a dozen languages and a 40% reduction in the main body price. Although the game is still small in scale and the peak online player count is only around ninety, you can clearly feel that the production team is gradually filling in the gaps and expanding the grand vision; every update log in the official community is filled with the clumsy enthusiasm of "Thank you all for accompanying me", making people's lips curl up involuntarily. Summary: This excellent game from the divine realm is a money-making gem. Playing it with friends is extremely enjoyable.

毫无疑问 这是一款十分优秀的塔防游戏 别出心裁的地图设计 优秀的人物以及各级建筑升级的设计 令人眼前一亮的美术设计 有趣的联机体验 这些优点足以让我给出对这款游戏很高的评价 看出制作组对这款游戏的用心 不过游戏上手难度还是有些高的 ui以及引导做的不是很好 难度对于刚刚接触这款游戏的人来说会有些高 不过随着对于游戏机制的不断探索 运用地形时间运营等各种要素 新手就能逐渐上手这款游戏 得出自己的公式打法 到时候绝大部分关卡都可以迎刃而解 这款游戏主打的应该还是联机体验的 跟朋友一块玩体验会非常好 选择不同角色承担不同责任合作过关的模式怎么说都不会过时 非常推荐这款游戏 小众宝藏塔防游戏 There is no doubt that this is an outstanding tower defense game. The unique map design, excellent character and building upgrade designs at each level, eye-catching art design, and interesting online experience are all advantages that are enough for me to give this game a high evaluation. It's obvious that the development team has put a lot of effort into this game. However, the game's learning curve is still a bit steep. The UI and guidance are not well done. The difficulty might be a bit high for those who are just getting started with this game. But as players keep exploring the game mechanics and make use of various elements such as terrain, time, and operation, newbies can gradually get the hang of it and develop their own formulaic strategies. Then, most of the levels can be easily tackled. This game should mainly focus on the online experience. Playing with friends will be a great experience. The mode where you choose different characters to take on different responsibilities and cooperate to pass levels will never go out of style. This game is highly recommended. It's a hidden gem of a tower defense game.

Note: I am rewriting this review to be less caustic and more informative. My frustrations remain. [hr][/hr] In terms of tower defense gameplay, the game is great. Challenging, but there are a lot of ways to experiment with your builds. The tools and vessels (characters with different tower options) you can unlock are fun, and are a nice part of your long term progression. The sound and visual effects are satisfying, as well as watching a good setup mow down an incoming enemy wave. If you enjoy tower defense games with economy elements, you will have fun playing this. [hr][/hr] Why is this review negative, then? I can't remember the last game I've played that had such a blatantly [b]hostile[/b] UI and UX. It is like the game actively protests against the very idea of being played. [h3]Readability and Contrast.[/h3] The game environment has a very bright color palette; a lot of whites and pale colors, and a lot of glassy transparent overlays. What color palette do you figure the devs decided on for the text and UI? White text, in a thin font with no outlines. You traverse to different stages by moving around a floating islands style overworld. It natually contains a lot of pale white clouds, along with pale white cliffs. You move around by clicking on these flying buoys, or in their direction if they're off-screen. If they're off-screen, lines will appear to indicate valid travel direction. These lines are just a pixel or two wide, have no outline, only appear in pulses every couple of seconds, and yes, they too are white. They are very easy to miss unless you tediously wait at every buoy you arrive at and look carefully for the white lines to pulse. There are some that are nearly impossible to see. There is a character who is themed around producing snow, and expending it to attack enemies and heal fortifications. His snow producing towers can be upgraded to launch the snow to different locations. What color do you think was chosen to indicate where these snow towers are aiming? It's glassy white again. On white snow. White snow that can make it impossible to read the thin white text. The two small arrows that indicate which tower or unit is selected? Glassy white. The sphere that shows you the range of towers you select? Glassy white. I'm not sure that any UI in this game is 100% opaque. This includes the settings menu. Did no one see this during development and think that this might be a problem? [h3]The "Flow"[/h3] I mentioned at the start that the game is challenging. You're going to fail a lot; you're going to fail yet more when shooting for a True Victory. Well, that's just part of the learning process, is all. Just need to restart the stage— There is no quick restart option. You must leave and enter the stage every time you want to attempt it. Entering a stage is a 20-second animation. Exiting the stage is another 8 seconds. Finishing a stage by winning or losing involves a similarly long end-of-round report that gradually reveals the text and other information. [b]None of the above can be skipped or sped up.[/b] I know that at least the longest animation, entering a stage, can be mostly skipped, because the tutorial does this. To design a game as challenging as this, and then to make the fail-learn-try-again loop as agrravatingly slow as this, is baffling. I don't want to wait another 30 seconds or so every time I want to adjust my strategy. A lot of motivation to keep trying is at risk when you lose, especially when you have to start fresh every time and completing a stage can take half an hour or more. Do not put obstacles in the way of the most important part of the player experience loop. Opening the ESC menu is another short animation. This crosses the line from stylistic to just feeling [i]unresponsive[/i]. [h3]Interface and Information[/h3] There's no active pause, and a number of enemies come at you fast, requiring quick reflexes and split second decision making on what to build next or upgrade. Problem: The way the game detects and determines what you're clicking on is extremely unreliable. Selection "hitboxes" seem to be 50% larger than what is visually indicated. It can be literally impossible to click on a tower that you otherwise have an unhindered line of sight to because there is another tower "in front" of it. You can adjust the elevation and yaw of the camera, but not the pitch. This means that you cannot change the camera to a more top-down view to make selection easier. I can only assume that this is to preserve the visual consistency of the 2D enemy and unit sprites. However, this is a detrimental solution to a [i]created[/i] problem. Mobile units can phase into adjacent towers, making selecting them impossible. For one character, her mobile units have flag icons above them that you can alternatively select. However, these have the same selection detection problems as stated before, and severely contribute to UI clutter. I find myself ending sessions of playing this game often because I simply just don't want to deal with the absolute slog of moment-to-moment navigation of the menus and UI. There's also the lack of "on-the-fly" meaningful information. Tower upgrades do not numerically indicate how they affect the stats of the tower ahead of time, and some of their descriptions do not even really tell you what they do at all. In a couple of cases this is meant for discovery; in most cases this just serves to arbitrarily withhold vital information from players. But not to fear, detailed information can be found in the game's Journal. For example, if I want to know what a Tier 4 upgrade for a specific tower does, numbers and all, all I have to do is: 1 - Open the pause menu (2+ second animation) 2 - Click on the Journal Icon 3 - Click on the "Vessel" category 4 - Click on the Vessel that owns that tower 5 - Scroll down and select the tower 6 - Scroll down and select the prerequisite Tier 1 upgrade 7 - Select the prerequisite Tier 2 upgrade 8 - Select the prerequisite Tier 3 upgrade 9 - Select the Tier 4 upgrade 10 - Enjoy the fruits of my labor (about three or so numbers that take a short moment to read) There are hotkeys to various actions. However, to see these hotkey tooltips, you need to hover your mouse over the UI buttons for about a whole second. This game's pace is not conducive to hovering your mouse over any buttons for a full second. The keybinds menu lists these as "Build Tower/Quick Action [1-5]". This is a rather inelegant way to communicate that Keys 1-4 are for building towers, and 5-6 are for selling and optionally whatever special ability your vessel has. Save us the pain and assign the Sell and ability actions to dedicated keybinds like all the UI designers that came before you. Besides, what are you going to do if modded (or even future) vessels have more or less tower options? Our muscle memory should be as vessel-agnostic as possible. I'll keep playing this from time to time, and I'll change this review to positive once the developers utilize the last three or so decades of collective UI/UX design knowledge. A lot of these issues border on being [i]accessibility[/i] concerns. It's a shame, because if the developers had actually listened to the overwhelmingly consistent feedback regarding these issues and addressed it, then I am confident that they could have launched with at least a Very Positive review score. You've got a good game here; but it's such a pain to actually play it.

The concept for this game is great, a 3D tower defense with RTS aspects. There are all unique characters with vastly different playstyles that are very creative. However, it is clear the devs did not playtest this with anyone other than themselves. The game is missing information you'd expect from normal tower defense games. Notably, the game doesn't tell you what kinds of enemies you'll expect in upcoming rounds, and some types are extremely punishing. It is very common for your resource node to be randomly attacked (which is extremely debilitating), or the boss simply having the ability to nuke an entire line of turrets, and results in unfair difficulty spikes. Nothing really teaches this, or my 2 friends playing co-op here all missed it with me. There are already many comments regarding UI and UX issues that make the game terrible to pick up already. I recommend that the devs get a UI/UX designer, and if they already have one, evaluate their competency because it is unbelievable that this game underwent early access and it is still in this state.

这是一款非常有趣的塔防游戏，但其设计并不适合单人游玩或大规模联机（4人及以上），最理想的游玩人数是2-3人。原因主要有两点：首先，游戏机制要求玩家建造防御塔来消灭敌人并保护己方的蓝色水晶塔，而建设防御塔所需的资源需要从地图中获取。每张地图的资源获取方式和效率各不相同，且资源会平均分配给所有玩家。在单人模式下，虽然玩家能获得100%的资源，但由于角色机制限制和操作压力（需要快速在多个位置部署防御塔），游戏体验会大打折扣；而当玩家过多时，人均资源分配过少，加上地图中适合建造防御塔的位置有限，反而会大幅提升通关难度。因此，2-3人的协作模式最能体现游戏的设计精髓。 新手阶段容易卡关是这款游戏的特色之一。玩家操控的角色和敌方单位存在显著的数值差距——常常需要用攻击力仅两位数的防御塔去消耗拥有上千血量的敌人。加之地图规模有限，想要在敌人行进途中快速歼灭几乎不可能。正是在无数次失败中，玩家才会逐渐领悟真正的通关策略，学会必要的技巧。这个探索过程恰恰展现了游戏机制的深度，每一个新发现都能带来独特的惊喜，这种持续的成就感正是推动我挑战所有关卡的动力。 游戏的美术设计尤为出色。在保持整体简约风格的同时，每张地图及其所属区块都拥有独特的设计，完美融入世界观。更值得一提的是环境机制的变化——不同区块会呈现完全不同的战术挑战。音乐同样是点睛之笔，每首OST都充满律动感，堪称游戏体验的灵魂所在。我强烈建议所有玩家开启音乐，这绝对会让冒险体验提升一个档次。 角色设计更是体现了开发者的巧思。每个角色的技能体系都逻辑自洽且具有精妙的联动效果（注：部分角色名称采用玩家间非官方称呼）。例如初始角色"小黄"专精资源采集而非直接输出；"小狗"的技能完美还原了犬类活泼好动的特性；而有“起床气”（乐）的"钓鱼猫哥"则拥有着极强的输出和机制。每个角色都蕴含着待开发的独特机制，正如前文所述，探索这些机制正是游戏的核心乐趣之一。

This game has 2 separate learning curves. Getting better at Strategy to more effectively use your Towers for Defense. A very fun and satisfying experience. What makes everything else worth putting up with. The other is learning to deal with the bizarre and cumbersome UI UX design that prioritises form above function that adamantly refused to change despite continuous community feedback over 2 years, map navigation being one of the greatest offenders. There is nothing wrong with having to learn a new game to get the most out it, but only 1 of these curves has anything to do with getting better at the game and gaining mastery. The other appears as though it's in opposition to the fundamental idea of letting you play the game. It's borderline disgraceful to pay money to enjoy a game and be met with such an obstacle. Every time I hear the initial experience of a friend trying the game, without fail there are always complaints with trying to understand what the game is telling them, how to play it and how to get into new levels. The design of the game is actively filtering out players that could potentially love the gameplay itself but are literally unable to reach this content as a result of the surrounding issues. How can I recommend a game that is guaranteed to give a bad first impression in its current state and potentially turn a player off the game forever?

Simply the best Tower Defense game I've ever played. The UI is confusing and counter intuitive, which is unfortunately the single complaint of the vast majority of the negative reviews. But you will get used to it if you stick it out and the game play more than makes up for it imo. The amount of depth and strategy in this game is in its own league. Like the game's description mentions, this is also a Real-Time Strategy game so there is resources you have to mine and manage in order to place your units. You're under a timer between each wave and enemies can kill you, so you can't always place towers whenever you feel like it, so you need to think ahead. There are very strong enemies, so you want to think about what upgrades your doing, usually spam placing towers last minute won't work. There are also buffs you can select before the game starts called Cardinals which gives you certain buffs and you can have multiple different types of Cardinals, which really opens up many more playstyles. This game also has "vessels" which are different characters with completely different units and play styles from each other. All of them require effective resource management and Real-Time-Strategy in order to clear the map. Also different maps don't just have different paths or design, they also have unique elements and rules which completely change the game and require you to strategize around. I would give examples, but the surprises are too good to spoil. You will inevitably fail to clear some maps, but the game still gives you rewards for partial wave clears making progression feel meaningful and satisfying. I was able to beat the game in about 25 hours but most maps I didn't fully clear, though I got very far and usually near the end. The game does have post game content which I've barely started but it's meaningfully different, so there's plenty of content in this game and I could easily see myself sinking 100s of hours into this game. I feel like there's still so much for me to learn and I've just scratched the surface. This game does have an easy mode which I highly recommend, especially for beginners as it gives you more room for mistakes while still challenging you (especially in higher difficulty maps). The game also has coop, which makes it so much more fun especially since you and your friends can go different characters. The enemies don't scale with number of players but you will be bottle necked by having to share the same resources so it ends up being a very balanced experience. Communication will be key in coop, so you can cover each others weaknesses and come up with synergies and combos to clear waves and harvest resources more effectively. Overall 9.5/10 for me, super unique game play with a lot of charm. I would recommend this to anyone who likes Tower Defense Games and if you like Real-Time Strategy games as well that just makes this a no brainer. Hopefully the UI continues to improve and this game becomes less confusing for beginners. This game is criminally underrated and more people need to hear about it.

The gameplay is pretty difficult unless you're playing cooperatively, which makes it a bit easier as you can actually synergize a bit. Map design is seemingly designed against the player, many maps are multi-layered with only a few seconds to understand pathing via a tiny almost transparent line that travels. One map straight up punishes you for not forseeing a lane change, not very play friendly of you map. Most maps give you a very narrow room for traditional tower defense placement, usually requiring you to just use the snowman to stall them. Infact the snoman is actually overpowered for defense when using healing heaters and thin walls, most of the time the snoman got me to wave 20-25 without really trying. Also on some maps there are stairs or ladders, putting walls near these without covering the entire edge to edge can result in them walking around, very funny of you game. UI design is artistic, and I mean artistic. In that its not designed to really be readable until you know what you're looking at. Many ui buttons are unlabeled and symbol only, I like reading to know what I'm about to press instead of guessing. Also the worst sin of game uis, you cant press escape to exit menus. Cutscenes/transitions are nice, but they are no skippable. This isn't a problem but when I don't care for a moment you have to just wait through maybe 10-15 seconds of transition everytime you get an item or unlock someone. Please just let me skip the cutscenes. Enemy balance is a bit funky since up to wave 20 is decently easy but then after that you are essentially boned if you do not have solid DPS and defense since it introduces a guy who will kill everything instantly in a 3x3 area after wave 20 something. While it is an upgrade of the previous version of him, the damage going from manageable to entire defense line shattered in seconds in like a few waves was a bit funny. Theres also the artillery guys who appear around wave 20 and so on that can do massive backline damage, keep in mind you cannot directly repair buildings so those buildings are essentially just damaged forever annoyingly. As for characters or vessels as they're called, the only one I found useful was the snoman with the other being the starter guy. When used together they are pretty solid for resource gathering and just building a solid defense. I've found some usage with the catman on some specific maps but didn't really like him that much. The knight you get later who can arm their knights with guns seems useful as a support but doesn't have many wall healing options despite getting a so called modular wall. My other minor complaint is that the current vessels seem lacking, theres like 1 generalist and 4 supports really, I've found only the starter guy to be good at collecting resources but I haven't done extensive testing since the game gives you no info. As for towers and upgrades, probably the most annoying part of the game. Unlike many other tower defenses, this game does not tell you what the next upgrade does, requiring you to waste resources to see if it will even help you at all. Ontop of that you cannot undo or swap upgrades, so you ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up trying to upgrade multiple towers now you have to sell it and start again. Also there is no tower copy and paste or upgrade path blueprint, so upgrading a million things gets a bit tedious. Another complaint is the snoman's sno launching requires you to individual re-aim each one... like please add a button to aim all or a select to aim a few cause re. (After more playthrough time, the most useful characters are sno sno then buster, Sno Sno can use snobbles and heater healed thin walls, decently op if combined with someone running damage with smacky. Buster is straight up busted, dogs deal damage when running through enemy, speed pads can make chainsaw setups or just run their path, enemies that want to damage units and towers will stop to damage dog and get damaged.) Overall, I am neutral about it, mostly because of how little information the game gives you. I'm all for experimentation but like experimentation is punished with how slow resource gain can be. If I'm going to experiment I don't want to just be killed for a mistake I can't really ta If you are going to play have a second person and be prepared for verticality cause many maps are multi-layer jungle gyms.

Really fun tower defense game, I've been a player of blockage games for a while now. The game's artstyle and music are really nice and give a really relaxing vibe, though later waves definitely can feel intense. I do agree with some complaints about the UI and experimentation definitely can feel discouraged when playing, but I don't find it too much of a problem personally. The game has a lot of content for a tower defense game, with more maps then I can count and five characters which all play very different from one another. It's also multiplayer, which I find isn't too common with these types of games, but I find a big bonus. A key mechanic that makes me really like this game are the Cardinals. Giving a roguelike-esque vibe, they give different bonuses to resource gathering, stats, or miscellaneous effects. Using them with different vessels and maps allow for numerous synergies and adds a layer of planning to the game before you even challenge a map. TLDR: Fun & Challenging tower defense game, multiplayer is nice, and lots of loadout diversity. WOULD RECOMMEND
